text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,144.3, down 0.61% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 fell 0.55%. Both indices were still in positive five‑day territory (+2.48% and +2.19% respectively), showing the move was limited to the top‑line decline. Advances‑declines were 157‑332, giving a breadth score of 75.7 and a “healthy” market‑wide sentiment, with about 82% of stocks above their 20‑day moving average.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added INR 5,736.55 crore, extending a 12‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 2,253.58 crore. The FII‑to‑DII net flow over the past five sessions was +16.9 crore. In options, Nifty’s put‑call ratio (PCR) is 0.83, indicating more call interest; the max‑pain level sits at 25,100 and the expected range is 24,911‑25,378. Bank Nifty’s PCR is 1.24, showing more put pressure, with max‑pain at 59,000 and an expected range of 60,001‑62,067. Call walls sit at 26,000 (Nifty) and 61,000 (Bank Nifty), while put walls are at 24,000 and 60,500 respectively.

Watch the 25,148.42 pivot (P) and the first support at 25,050.48 for Nifty; a break below could test the 24,911 level. Bank Nifty’s pivot is 61,038.4 with support at 60,776.25 – a move through this may target the 60,500 put wall. Key headlines to monitor include global risk cues (Nvidia earnings, Fed policy) and domestic earnings updates, which could influence the next session’s direction.
